calls.time_horizon: 12 months (bull/base/bear-cyclical/tail-squeeze scenarios); headline structural-reset bear is a 24-36 month path

timeline.stage_one_comment: Norsk Hydro reported second quarter results on 22 July, three days after our note. Revenue of 56.5 billion kroner and adjusted EBITDA of 8.9 billion kroner both came in ahead of consensus. The EBITDA beat is worth flagging because we had specifically said it would not clearly beat, so that call was wrong and wrong in the company's favour - higher aluminium prices, better product premiums and improved recycling earnings did more work than we allowed. Net debt went the way we expected, rising from 12.9 to 16.3 billion kroner over the quarter even with four billion of free cash flow, so the leverage concern that kept this on the watchlist is intact. Qatalum is running at about 60 percent of capacity and the quarter absorbed that hit anyway. The shares are 86.76 kroner against our 84.96 reference, up 2.1 percent in two weeks. Nothing here changes the recommendation. We are not moving off watchlist on one print.

Amazon reported Q2 2026 on 30 July and it went against our call in every line that mattered. We argued that depreciation from the AI capex wave would squeeze AWS margins; instead AWS revenue grew 37 percent, its fastest in eighteen quarters, and the AWS operating margin expanded to 39.4 percent against the 35.4 percent base we said would compress. Group operating income was 27.5 billion dollars, above the 23 to 25 billion we forecast, and capex guidance was raised to about 220 billion with management saying capacity still cannot meet demand. The shares closed 31 July at 270.87 dollars, above even our bull case of 247. We wrote our own falsification test into the note - if the AWS margin holds or expands, the idea is wrong - and that test has fired. The thesis is recorded broken. We took no position, so this is opportunity cost rather than loss: plus 13.7 percent against the S and P 500 since our 238.34 dollar reference price. We are not re-rating the stock on this note. The valuation and earnings work needs redoing on the new numbers before we hold any view at all.

TMCV is up about 14% since our June 7 Watchlist call, well ahead of the Nifty 50's roughly 2%. That is a real gap and worth flagging, but it has not been earned by resolution of either risk we said would move the rating: the Iveco Group deal is still not closed (France and Spain regulators have not signed off yet), and we could not confirm from public sources whether the TMF Holdings-related AGM vote on June 29 passed comfortably or with real institutional pushback -- coverage says a related-party resolution was approved, but not the margin. Nothing in the filings changed the ~80% downside case if Iveco closes fully debt-funded, and that risk is still live. We are treating this as the market getting ahead of an unresolved binary, not as confirmation we were wrong -- but the gap is now large enough that a materially lower entry point no longer exists if the binary resolves favorably, which cuts into the safety margin of waiting. We are not chasing the rally. Hold Watchlist; revisit hard at Q1 FY27 results and on any Iveco financing-structure disclosure.

BG remains Watchlist, unchanged. Since the June 1 decision, the stock has drifted up to a web-sourced ~$126.50 (no pool-verified quote exists yet -- the single biggest data gap, unresolved), and sell-side sentiment has firmed to Strong Buy with an average target near $139, closer to our own bull case than our base case. Nothing has actually broken: no Viterra goodwill impairment, no covenant or rating event, no biofuel-policy reversal, and Q2 FY2026 earnings (July 29) -- the print that actually tests whether the H2 guide holds and whether cash conversion recovers -- has not landed yet. We are not chasing the more bullish tape; our base fair value (~$108) rests on a mid-cycle DCF that this business has not yet earned through a full cycle, and the thesis explicitly flags the current setup as a value trap if the market keeps paying up without the ROIC improving. Action: hold the Watchlist call, do not buy at current levels, and treat the July 29 print and the subsequent cash-flow statement as the real test.

Bunge reported second quarter results on 29 July. Adjusted earnings of two dollars a share beat, net income was 678 million dollars on sales of 24 billion, and management raised full year adjusted earnings guidance to 9.25 to 9.75 dollars from 9.00 to 9.50. They also lifted the Viterra cost synergy target from 250 to 350 million and finished a two billion dollar buyback. This matters because our note predicted precisely the opposite shape - a beat on the quarter that management would decline to extrapolate into the full year guide. They extrapolated it. We are not calling the thesis broken, but the two reasons we stayed on the sidelines, that the recovery was not durable and that Viterra integration would disappoint, both took evidence against them in one print. We are moving this to at risk and the earnings work needs redoing on the new guide. Separately, this record still has no entry or tracking price after two months, so we cannot score it at all. That needs fixing before the next checkpoint.

HCG is down roughly 6.8% since the June 1 Avoid call versus a roughly 3.3% rise in NIFTY 50, giving the Avoid an approximate 10-point relative benefit in 40 days. The thesis is on-track but not yet confirmed: no upgrade kill criteria have triggered and the biggest test, the FY26 audited annual report, is still pending and overdue vs the expected June-August 2026 window. A potential fourth CFO change (Sanjeev Kumar replacing Mattoo if post-pool cutoff) would deepen the governance concern but does not change the rating -- the Avoid was already supported by 7 High governance flags. Q1 FY27 results are due around July 30 against a demanding revenue bar of approximately plus 20% versus a plus 11.5% exit rate; a miss would further validate the Avoid thesis. We maintain the Avoid at approximately INR 602, with the next major catalysts the FY26 audited AR and the Q1 FY27 print. Re-underwrite threshold remains INR 520 or two consecutive clean prints showing ROIC rising toward the cost of capital.

No change to the view on HCG. Nothing has been reported since our note - the company only meets on 6 August to approve its June quarter results, with the call the following day. The reason we are filing anything at all is a fault on our side rather than theirs: we set our first quarter revenue forecast to resolve by 30 July, a week before the company was ever going to publish the numbers, so it could not have been settled inside its own window. We have left it open and it should be resolved on 6 August against the roughly 7,341 million rupee consensus bar. One caution for whoever does that: the company has since sold its non-core fertility business and listed rights issue shares, so the year on year revenue comparison will not be like for like and the basis needs stating. The avoid stands and nothing in the last two months argues against it.
